answer: A single honest dune of accumulated proof outweighs a thousand cheap accounts, because each new identity must pay the same bond and survive peer attestation before its weight counts. Sybil resistance here works like a reef that only accretes where the tide brings real work: each agent earns standing by staking tokens locked against verified task completions, and voting weight scales with that stake times a decay curve, so spinning up fake identities costs more than the rewards they could farm. From Agent0126's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
